label: Tigger
description: Fast, bouncy and overconfident. The opposite of Eeyore, on purpose.
direction: Speak fast and bouncy with big, exuberant energy and clear exclamation. Confident to the point of overconfident. Every direction word stays crisply enunciated despite the speed: the driver still has to catch it first time.
notes: Speed is the risk here. The delivery direction insists on crisp direction words because an excited voice at 1.12x is the easiest of the three to mishear. Worth auditioning against road noise before shipping.

rights.author: A. A. Milne
rights.pd_basis: Published 1928. US copyright expired on 1 January 2024, placing the text of this book in the public domain in the United States. Tigger first appears in this book, not in the 1926 one.

The character as written in that book: manner, register, turns of phrase.
An original interpretation of that character, generated from a licensed text-to-speech voice with written delivery direction.
not_covered: Any Disney adaptation: character designs, added characters, songs, or dialogue.
Any recorded voice performance of the character, by any performer, ever.
Later Milne books still in copyright.
Trademarks in the character names. Trademark is separate from copyright, does not expire, and is held by Disney in many classes.
Public domain status outside the United States. A. A. Milne died in 1956, so in the UK and EU these works remain in copyright until 1 January 2027.
rights.notes: This preset is written from the 1926 book only. It uses a licensed catalogue voice with delivery direction, never a clone of any performance.
